top_strength: Airtight pricing/clock/estimate block — hit every differentiator (No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, full no-hidden-fees pitch) in one clean pass, then tied the 3-4 hour estimate to the specific variables driving it (freight elevator, ~80ft/two-bus walk, partial one-bedroom volume) instead of giving a generic range, while building real rapport with a returning customer (shared laugh over his decade-old TV).
coaching_note: Biggest miss is Section 6 — the full Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped entirely, a 10-point gap that matters most here since prep is exactly what keeps actual time inside the quoted window (ties directly to the estimate-accuracy push). Tighten the open with an explicit agenda statement + 'sound good?', use Patrick's name more than once, close with hours/how-to-reach-us instead of just 'reach out,' and flag the Home Depot box purchase as an Ecobox referral moment.
phone_presence_notes: Genuine warmth and easy back-and-forth throughout (the shared laugh over the old TV, casual asides about Texas heat), and the customer closed by thanking Bree by name and praising the team as 'really great and really professional and really efficient' — a returning customer explicitly delighted with the rep.
